title: Clean and Split Text
content:
What problem does this solve?
Real text often arrives with extra spaces, inconsistent capitalization, or separators between fields. String methods let you clean and divide that text.

One method at a time
strip() returns a string without surrounding whitespace. lower() returns a lowercase string. split(separator) returns a list of pieces.

Save the returned value
These methods do not rewrite the original string in place. If you need the cleaned value later, assign it or return it.

Chaining after understanding the steps
  clean = text.strip().lower()
means: first call strip(), receive the returned string, then call lower() on that returned string.

Vocabulary after the behavior
A method is a function called through a value with dot syntax. Strings are immutable here: methods return new string values instead of changing the original string object.
concepts: strip returns a string without surrounding whitespace
split returns a list of pieces
String-cleaning methods return new values rather than changing the original string in place
Method chaining feeds one returned value into the next method call

examples.title: Strip
examples.explanation: clean stores the new string without outside spaces.

examples.title: Split
examples.explanation: split returns a list containing the two fields.

examples.title: Chain after understanding
examples.explanation: strip returns a string, then lower is called on that returned value.

common_mistakes: Calling strip/lower but discarding the returned value
Thinking split returns a string instead of a list
Chaining many methods before being able to explain each intermediate result
Calling this NLP tokenization instead of ordinary Python text processing

exercises.title: Strip outside spaces
hints: strip removes whitespace only from the outside edges.
The brackets are added by the f-string after strip returns hello.
The exact output is [hello].

exercises.title: Lowercase a value
hints: lower returns a new lowercase string.
Every letter is converted to lowercase in the returned value.
The output is python.

exercises.title: Split into pieces
hints: split uses | as the boundary between pieces.
The returned value is a list, so printing it shows list brackets and quoted strings.
The output is ['Ada', 'Scout'].

exercises.title: Chain two simple steps
hints: First remove the outside spaces, then lowercase the returned string.
Both operations return strings, so the second can be called directly after the first.
Use `text.strip().lower()`.

exercises.title: Original and returned string
hints: lower returns a new value assigned to clean.
The original variable text still refers to HELLO.
The lines are HELLO, then hello.

exercises.title: Save the returned string
exercises.prompt: The final output should be `open gate`. Repair the code so the cleaned result is actually kept.
exercises.starter_code:
command = "  OPEN GATE  "
command.strip()
command.lower()
print(command)
exercises.reference_solution:
command = "  OPEN GATE  "
command = command.strip().lower()
print(command)
hints: The method calls currently produce values that are immediately discarded.
Assign the cleaned returned string back to command (or through an intermediate variable).
Use `command = command.strip().lower()` before printing.

exercises.title: Clean a status
exercises.prompt: Write `clean_status(text)` that returns the text with surrounding whitespace removed and letters converted to lowercase. Do not print inside the function.
hints: Return the cleaned text rather than printing it.
Apply strip and lower to the parameter; chaining is fine now that each step is understood.
Return `text.strip().lower()`.

exercises.title: Parse One Log Line
exercises.prompt: Write `parse_log_line(line)` for a well-formed `name|status` line. Split on `|`, trim both fields, lowercase only the status, and return exactly `{"name": <clean name>, "status": <clean lowercase status>}`. Malformed-line validation comes later.
hints: Split once conceptually first: the result is a two-item list.
Clean parts[0] with strip; clean parts[1] with strip then lower.
Return one dictionary with the two required keys after cleaning the two pieces.
exercises.success_message: One messy text line now becomes a clean structured record using only ordinary Python string and collection skills.
